text:
Three people were killed in a plane crash near the northern rim of Grand Canyon national park in Arizona, the federal park service said on Monday.
The Grand Canyon regional communications center received a report of a missing Piper Comanche aircraft at about 11.30pm on Sunday, a statement from officials said. The plane was last known to be in the Basin area of the park’s North Rim, a higher-elevation and less-visited section of the park.
Search crews began looking for the aircraft in the early morning hours on Monday. Officials said they located the wreckage and a debris field in the Basin area at about 10.15am on Monday. All three people onboard the aircraft were killed.
The National Park Service (NPS) has not released the victims’ identities, saying that was out of respect for their families.
According to officials, the crashed aircraft was found after the Arizona department of public safety conducted an aerial search using night vision and forward-looking infrared technology. Coconino county search and rescue, Kane county search and rescue, and the air force rescue coordination center also assisted with the operation.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) will investigate the cause of the crash with assistance from the NPS, officials added.
The area where the crash occurred sits between 8,000 and 8,800 feet (2.4 and 2.7km) above sea level, about 1,000 feet (305 meters) higher than the South Rim.
digest_he: שלושה בני אדם נהרגו בהתרסקות מטוס קל מסוג פייפר קומאנצ'י סמוך לשוליים הצפוניים של הפארק הלאומי גרנד קניון באריזונה. מרכז התקשורת האזורי קיבל דיווח על מטוס נעדר, וצוותי חיפוש והצלה איתרו את ההריסות באזור הבסין באמצעות טכנולוגיית ראיית לילה ואינפרא-אדום. שירות הפארקים הלאומיים והמועצה הלאומית לבטיחות בתעבורה צפויים לחקור את נסיבות התאונה, כאשר זהויות הקורבנות טרם פורסמו מתוך כבוד למשפחותיהם.
